READ FIRST, in this order — binding contract:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — tokens, components, and an AUDITED table of what does NOT exist. Read the whole thing.
2. `app/globals.css` — "KODELY PRODUCT SURFACE" and "PRODUCT UTILITIES" blocks.

4. `components/app/AppShell.tsx`, `app/(portal)/layout.tsx` — your pages render CONTENT ONLY.
5. `lib/credits.ts` IN FULL, `lib/stripe.ts`, `app/(portal)/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` + `ledger.ts`, `app/api/billing/**`.

YOU OWN: `app/(portal)/dashboard/billing/**` and `app/(portal)/dashboard/usage/**` (new). Do NOT touch anything else — other agents own the rest of the portal in parallel. You may READ `app/(portal)/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx` and import it, but not edit it.

## THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — read this twice

The brief I was given asks for "Kodely Pro, $XX/month, next billing date, payment method Visa ••••4242, invoice history, plan comparison Free/Pro/Business".

**None of that exists.** The audit is unambiguous:
- There is NO subscription, NO plan, NO price, NO renewal date. Checkout runs in one-off `payment` mode for credit packs (`lib/stripe.ts:44-48` — starter 500/$9, builder 2500/$40, pro 6000/$90).
- Payment method is never read back from Stripe; only `User.stripeCustomerId` is stored.
- There is NO invoice history — no Stripe invoice fetch anywhere. The append-only `CreditLedger` is the only history that exists.
- Credits **never expire**. There is no monthly allowance and **no reset date** — the spend cap is deliberately a *rolling* 30 days precisely so there is no reset day (`lib/credits.ts:258-262`).
- Storage and bandwidth are **not measured anywhere**.

**Do not invent any of it.** Your job is to build the best possible billing and usage experience out of what is genuinely there — which is actually quite a lot — and to state plainly where something does not exist. Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"`. A page that says "Kodely bills per build, not per month — here is exactly where your credits went" is a *better* page than a fake subscription screen, and it is the truth.

## TASK 1 — Usage (`/dashboard/usage`, new)

Real and available:
- Balance via `getBalance()`; rolling-30-day spend via `spentInWindow()`; `averageBuildCredits()` over the last 10 charged builds.
- Per-build cost: `Build.costMicros`, `Build.creditsCharged`, `Build.repairAttempts`.
- **Per-website attribution is real and already joined**: `CreditLedger.buildId → Build.projectId`, and the existing billing page already renders the project name per ledger row. A per-site rollup is a `groupBy` away, no schema change. Caveat: deleting a project SET NULLs `buildId`, so attribution is lost for deleted sites — the existing page already handles this, match its honesty.
- Usage over time is derivable from `CreditLedger.createdAt`.

Build: clear headline numbers, a per-website breakdown, and a usage-over-time chart. **Chart with no dependency** — hand-rolled inline SVG or CSS. Give it the same care as the type: real axis labels, a readable empty state, and it must work in both themes and be keyboard/screen-reader accessible (a table fallback is a legitimate and good answer). Explain what credits were spent ON, not just how many.

Also surface the spend cap here (`getSpendCapStatus`) — it is the one real control over usage. Do not duplicate the form if another page owns it; link to it.

## TASK 2 — Billing (`/dashboard/billing`)

Rebuild it on the design system. Keep every honest thing the current page does — read it carefully first, it is already careful — and improve the presentation:
- Credit packs and checkout (gated on `billingEnabled()`, which needs BOTH `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`).
- The credit statement with its existing paging.
- The spend cap.
- When `billingEnabled()` is false, the statement must still render — the current page is deliberate about this (`app/(portal)/dashboard/page.tsx:45-48` explains why) and you must preserve that.

HARD RULES:
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.**
- No new npm dependencies. Server Components by default.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element. `k-num` on EVERY figure — this page is nothing but figures. `k-scroll-x` on the statement table.
- Harden paging/query params with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` — never `x in OBJ`.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on your paths with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.

REPORT BACK concisely: what you built, exactly which requested items you refused to fake and what you showed instead, your charting approach and its accessibility story, and anything untested.

59	
60	## Utility classes
61	
62	`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`.
101	
102	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
103	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
108	
109	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
110	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
111	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
112	
113	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
114	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
115	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
116	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
117	and not a progress bar.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
122	
123	| Thing | Reality |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
126	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
127	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
128	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
129	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
130	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
131	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
132	| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
133	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
134	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
135	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
136	
137	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, ARE cheaply real** — the
138	`Session` model is per-user and queryable.
139	
140	### The rule
141	
142	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
143	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
144	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

Welcome to the Next.js documentation!

## What is Next.js?

Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.

It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.

Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.

## How to use the docs

The docs are organized into 3 sections:

- [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
- [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
- [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.

Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.

## App Router and Pages Router

Next.js has two different routers:

- **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
- **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.

At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.

### React version handling

The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:

- **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.

- **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.

This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.

## Pre-requisite knowledge

Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:

- HTML
- CSS
- JavaScript
- React

If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.

## Accessibility

For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.

## Join our Community

If you have questions about anything related to Next.js, you're always welcome to ask our community on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions), [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/bUG2bvbtHy), [X (Twitter)](https://x.com/nextjs), and [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/nextjs).

content.text:
Both pages are built, verified against the live dev server with real data, and clean on `tsc` + `eslint`.

## Files

| Path | |
|---|---|
| `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\usage\page.tsx` | new |
| `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\usage\data.ts` | new — all aggregation |
| `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\usage\UsageChart.tsx` | new — the chart |
| `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\billing\page.tsx` | rebuilt on the design system |
| `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\billing\SpendCapPanel.tsx` | new — shared by both pages |
| `C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod\app\(portal)\dashboard\billing\ledger.ts` | added `formatUsdCents` (retail only) |

Nothing outside `billing/**` and `usage/**` was touched. The old billing page rendered its own `<main id="main-content">` nested inside `AppShell`'s `<main>`; both pages now render content only.

## What I refused to fake, and what I showed instead

- **Plan / price / renewal date** → one `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` at the foot of billing: *"There is no plan, invoice or saved card to show"*, stating there is no tier, no monthly price, nothing to downgrade.
- **Payment method (Visa ••••4242)** → same panel: card details stay with Stripe, Kodely never reads them back and cannot display a last-four. Only `stripeCustomerId` is stored.
- **Invoice history** → same panel: no Stripe invoice is ever fetched; the credit statement is the complete record.
- **Plan comparison Free/Pro/Business** → replaced with a real pack comparison table built from `CREDIT_PACKS`: credits, price, price per credit, and *"about N builds"* from that user's own measured average (that last column shows `—` until they have a charged build rather than dividing by the global fallback constant).
- **Credit reset date** → stated three times as absent; the cap panel explains the rolling window has no reset day and no cliff.
- **Storage / bandwidth** → `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` at the foot of usage.
- **Cost basis** → a self-imposed refusal: `Build.costMicros` is our model spend and the cost side of the margins in `lib/stripe.ts`. It is used only inside arithmetic in `data.ts` and never rendered as money. Every figure on both pages is in credits.

## What is real and now shown

Usage: balance, rolling-30-day spend, measured average build, affordable builds; a per-website rollup (`Build.groupBy` by `projectId` with credits/build count/last-charged/share bar) plus an explicit **"Websites you've deleted"** row reconciling the ledger total against attributable builds — deletion cascades builds away and SET NULLs `buildId`, so those charges genuinely cannot be attributed; and **"What you weren't charged for"**: failed-build count, repaired-build count, and credits absorbed on repairs, derived exactly as `lib/credits.ts` says it can be (`repairAttempts > 0` and `costMicros > creditsCharged * MICROS_PER_CREDIT`). That derivation rounds *down* on purpose, since `creditsCharged` is ceil-rounded — understating what we absorbed is the only safe direction on this page.

Billing keeps everything the old page did (statement paging, cap, packs, the estimate brackets and their two-samples caveat) and adds the second statement line `lib/credits.ts` recommends: **"Needed a repair pass — you weren't charged for it."** The statement still renders in full when `billingEnabled()` is false — verified, since Stripe is not configured on this deployment.

## Chart and its accessibility story

Hand-rolled inline SVG in a Server Component — zero JS shipped, no dependency. Colours are Tailwind classes bound to design tokens (`fill-brand`, `stroke-hair`, `fill-ink-3`), never attributes or hex, so both themes come free from the same variable swap. Uniform `viewBox` scaling, so no label ever clips. Three channels: a prose `<figcaption>` summary; `role="img"` with an `aria-label` carrying that summary (so a screen reader gets the shape, not 30 unlabelled rects); and a real `<table>` in a keyboard-operable `<details>` carrying every figure, in `k-scroll-x`. Bars are deliberately not individually focusable *because* the table exists. Empty window gets a readable `EmptyState`. Range is 30/90 days via `?range=`, hardened with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` against a closed table — verified that `?range=__proto__` falls back to 30.

Also hardened: `?page=` on billing, same way.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: zero errors in my paths. (Pre-existing errors elsewhere from parallel agents: `app/(portal)/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx`, and `PreviewFrame.tsx` importing a missing `./BuildVeil`.)
- `npx eslint --max-warnings=0` on both directories: clean.
- Every Tailwind class I introduced (`min-w-xl`, `fill-brand`, `stroke-hair`, `divide-hair`, …) compiled through the project's own Tailwind config to confirm it emits.
- Both pages rendered 200 against the running dev server on :3003 with a real account (7 builds, 3 ledger rows). Verified the stat row, cap panel, chart geometry (gridlines, bar height, axis label positions all inside the viewBox), table fallback, per-site rollup, statement, and paging. I created a 10-minute session row to do this and deleted it afterwards — confirmed removed.

## Untested

- The `billingEnabled() === true` branch of "Add credits" (the pack table + `TopUpButton` with real packs). Stripe is not configured on this deployment, so only the disabled branch was exercised. It type-checks and reads from `CREDIT_PACKS` directly.
- Three data-dependent branches with no data on this account: a **set** spend cap, the **deleted-sites** row, and the **repair-waived** statement line.
- No visual/browser screenshot — every browser tab was in use by parallel agents and I did not want to navigate one out from under them. Verification was on rendered HTML and SVG geometry instead.

One thing worth flagging: `TopUpButton` is the only purchase affordance on the billing page and I could not edit it, so the primary money action renders as a small underlined link in the old style rather than a design-system button. I gave it a bordered section and surrounding context, but it is visibly from the previous system. Whoever owns that file should port it.
